newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to deport first batch of illegal workers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to deport first batch of illegal workers.

text.p: Malaysia will begin deporting 700,000 illegal workers on Friday, with about 2,000 Indonesians scheduled to be repatriated on an Indonesian naval ship, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.

The Tanjung Osina is expected to leave the southern state of Johor with the Indonesians from seven holding camps in various parts of Malaysia, Bernama said, quoting Indonesian consul Bachrun Subardjo.
Illegal foreign workers make up about one-eighth of the country's eight million-strong workforce.

A three-month amnesty for about one million illegal workers to register with the government expired on Tuesday -- the last day of 1996 -- and about 70 percent of them missed the exercise and looked set to be deported, immigration officials said.
Malaysian petrol pumps on Wednesday began a national campaign to reduce dependence on foreign labour by introducing self-service.
About 8,000 Bangladeshi migrant workers manning petrol pumps across Malaysia face the prospect of being replaced by the new self-service system.

"The problem of unskilled workers is very rampant in our country and most of the (petrol) stations, especially in major towns, employ foreign workers," Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Abu Hassan Omar told a news conference.
"Therefore, this is also an attempt by the government to reduce the number of foreign workers," he said at the launch of the self-service system on Wednesday.
Malaysia's booming economy has created acute labour shortages in the country of 20 million people and provided a magnet for foreign workers.

Indonesians and Philippine nationals have been recruited over the years to work as house maids and as construction, plantation and restaurant hands, while Bangladeshis have been employed as petrol pump attendants.
About 300,000 illegal immigrants registered with the government during the three-month amnesty.
